title: Ulyana and the Orbit
premise: Wendell Ashgrove has spent eleven years alone aboard Relay Station Kestrel, tending a beacon whose original commissioning orders were lost in the Collapse. When the deep-space vessel Meridian returns with a crew aged backward into childhood, Wendell discovers the beacon is not a navigation aid but a countdown — and its signal is all that keeps two hostile fleets from converging on the station. To buy time, she fabricates an authority that never existed, inventing 'Commander Ashgrove' as the station's missing founder while raising the Meridian's de-aged crew as her own found family. In the end, Wendell must choose between preserving the lie that holds the peace and revealing herself; she broadcasts the truth, adopts the beacon's purpose as her own inheritance, and the fleets stand down when the children of the Meridian speak for her.
about_author: Bram Ashgrove is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent a decade maintaining remote listening posts in the subarctic before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness, inherited machines, and the families people build in the margins of vast systems.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Establishing her solitary routine aboard Kestrel: calibrating the ancient beacon, talking to the station AI, mourning a career that ended in exile. She finds a sealed maintenance log older than her assignment, hinting the beacon predates every record. Emotional beat: quiet ache of purpose without provenance.

chapters.title: Return Signal
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A ship appears on long-range scopes — the Meridian, lost forty years ago, transponders matching but hull scorched by relativistic travel. Docking clamps engage on their own. Wendell opens the airlock to find thirty-one children where a veteran crew should be. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, intercut with eight-year-old Sefa, the Meridian's former captain. The children remember being adults; their bodies disagree. Wendell improvises care, rationing, routines — becoming, uncomfortably, a parent overnight. The oldest child warns her: they were running from something. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Counts
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Decoding the sealed log, she learns the beacon emits a false fleet-identification pulse; if it falters, two armadas will read the sector as unclaimed and converge. The countdown is tied to the Meridian's return — someone designed it this way. Emotional beat: vertigo of inherited responsibility.

chapters.title: Commander Ashgrove
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. To answer a fleet hail, she invents the station's founder: Commander Wendell Ashgrove, voice synthesized, credentials forged from the log's fragments. Both fleets accept the fiction. The lie works — and begins demanding more of her. Emotional beat: intoxication and guilt of self-invention.

chapters.title: Sefa Remembers the War
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The de-aged captain recalls why the Meridian fled: her crew refused an order to fire on the second fleet, most of whom are their own kin. Sefa recognizes the beacon's pulse pattern — she helped design it, adult hands in a child's memory. Emotional beat: grief outliving the body that earned it.

chapters.title: Interrogation at Light-Lag
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Fleet One sends an inspector, delayed by light-lag politics, demanding proof Commander Ashgrove exists. Wendell stages the empty station as a living command, coaching the children to play crew. The inspector grows suspicious of a commander never seen. Emotional beat: performance under pressure, found family as alibi.

chapters.title: The Countdown Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The beacon's core fails; her forged identity unravels as both fleets detect the gap and begin moving. The children, terrified, blame her lie. Wendell confesses everything — no commander, no orders, only a technician who stayed. Emotional beat: collapse of the false self, raw honesty.

chapters.title: Thirty-One Voices
chapters.summary: POV Sefa, then Wendell. Climax. Instead of restoring the deception, Wendell opens an open channel and lets the Meridian's children speak — living evidence of what the war would cost. Sefa addresses both fleets as their former captain. Fleets hold position. Emotional beat: truth as stronger armor than lies.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, epilogue months later. The fleets establish joint custody of Kestrel; the beacon is rebuilt openly, its purpose documented at last. Wendell signs the maintenance log as its first honest entry, the children's names beside hers. She is no longer the last human on the station — she is its keeper. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen and earned.
